<article class="reference-handbook">
<p class="pg-lede">Reference data handbooks collect technical parameters and model inputs with their values, bases, original sources and reuse terms. They help researchers find and cite the source behind each number.</p>
<p>This is not a harmonized forecast or a collection of study results. Historical status, targets, reference designs, model assumptions and observations retain their source-specific bases. Costs are not escalated to current dollars.</p>
<section class="fx-sec" aria-labelledby="handbooks">
<div class="fx-head"><h2 id="handbooks">Handbooks</h2></div>
<div class="card ref-card theme-hydrogen"><h3><a href="hydrogen.html">Hydrogen techno-economic parameters and inputs</a></h3>
<p>Version 0.1 · 76 quantities · 66 handbook IDs · checked 2026-11-13</p>
<p>Electrolysis, storage and delivery, compression, fuel cells, fossil-hydrogen comparisons, policy and market inputs.</p></div>
<p>Planned: wind, solar, nuclear/SMR, storage, markets.</p>
</section>
<section class="fx-sec" aria-labelledby="cite">
<div class="fx-head"><h2 id="cite">How to cite</h2></div>
<p>Cite the compilation, the original source of every numerical input (including its table or page and version), and Henry’s paper when reproducing that paper’s assumptions or model configuration. A numerical correspondence does not establish adoption of the same source.</p>
<p class="ref-citation">Li, H. (2026). Hydrogen techno-economic parameters and inputs: Reference data handbook. Version 0.1. https://henryutd2021.github.io/reference-data/hydrogen.html. Accessed [date], records [IDs].</p>
<p>Use the versioned CSV and record IDs to identify the inputs used. The compilation citation credits curation and does not replace original-source citations.</p>
</section>
<section class="fx-sec" aria-labelledby="licence">

</section>

<p>Future releases will keep versioned downloads, record changes in the change log and update the latest CSV. See the <a href="hydrogen.html#updates">source review schedule</a>.</p>
